is: The HTTP driving adapter over `composition::Runtime`: the axum router, the RFC 9457 error shape, the generated wire contract, the session layer, and the one background task — handlers are thin drivers over the shared `application::*` use cases (`commissions/channel` + `commissions/elements` still await a use case, and `session`'s sign-in provisioning still opens its own unit of work).
conventions: Two endpoint shapes coexist — the browser sign-in flow redirects; every JSON API returns status codes (401, never a redirect).
Errors are `application/problem+json` with a `urn:zurfur:error:*` type and terse code.

A namespace boundary is a policy boundary: cookie-surface routers sit under the first-party-Origin CSRF layer; `/health`, `/.well-known` and a future bearer `/plugin/v1` mount outside it by construction, and a path no route matches gets a bare 404 from the outer router's own fallback, outside it too.
Session→identity resolution is one axum extractor, `extract::CallingUser`, never a per-module helper.
Parity tests (`create_account_parity.rs`, `delete_account_parity.rs`, `whoami_parity.rs`) pin this driver's projections identical to the CLI's until the contract moves to a leaf crate.

The `dev-profile` Cargo feature alone chooses the dev profile (never config or `.env`). Two locks: `main` refuses unless `ZURFUR_ENV` is set and names dev, and `dev_profile::app` refuses a resolved environment other than `DEV`, both before anything starts; `Config::load` before them refuses a DEV listening, or served, beyond loopback. `just gate`, gate-light and CI lint and test the feature in `target/dev-profile` (so `target/debug/api` is never the profile), pinned by `scripts/dev-profile-pins.test.sh`.

A driver: it never names the node port, `WriteCapability` or its issuer, adapter-mem's commission seeders (`seed_bound_commission`, `seed_stored_title`, `seed_lifecycle_step`, `seed_tab`, `seed_participant`, `remove_participant`: the dev profile seeds only through the fixture), `adapter_pg::queries` or `sqlx`, nor holds a string literal naming the `node` table (application/tests/write_gate_seams.rs, over every crate cargo metadata finds depending on composition). The one exemption is `sweep.rs`'s `sweep_pass_as_leader`, whose advisory lock may name `sqlx` once, until ARC-3 moves it. Its calls on a unit's `commissions()` and `changelog()` are held by clippy.toml instead, each with its own `#[expect]`.

fs.name: Cargo.toml
fs.role: wires domain + adapter-pg + composition + application + shared, http-stack for the served stack, tokio-util/futures-util for upload streaming glue (adapter-mem/test-support/contract-gen/cli as dev-deps); sqlx only for the sweeper's advisory lock; the `dev-profile` feature (off by default) makes adapter-mem a real dependency and builds the dev profile into the binary

fs.name: clippy.toml
fs.role: large-error-threshold 192 (Problem with field errors); disallowed-methods: tower_sessions::SessionManagerLayer::new (sessions mount only through http_cookies::session_layer), axum::serve (serving only through http_stack::serve), UnitOfWork::nodes (no driver reaches the Den's node port; the delegating double in tests/commission_delete.rs carries an `#[expect]`), WriteCapability::gate_issued (only the den's write gate issues one), and, the interim guard until ARC-4, UnitOfWork::commissions and UnitOfWork::changelog (the six calls left in routes/commissions/channel.rs and elements.rs each carry an `#[expect]` on its statement, as do the doubles and seeders in tests/commission_delete.rs, commission_positioning.rs and commission_elements.rs)

fs.name: src/
fs.role: lib/main, logging (the server subscriber with the shared DNS-client filter), extractors, routes, problem, sweep, generated contract types

fs.name: tests/
fs.role: ~40 flat integration suites over reqwest (accounts, commissions/*, csrf (the CSRF matrix on bare clients: no signal on every write the API serves (paths read from each `.route(` in src/, which fails on a `.nest(`, `.nest_service(`, `.route_service(` or a non-literal path; methods from axum's Allow on a first-party PROPFIND; only GET, HEAD and OPTIONS left out; every escaped route named), foreign, null or empty Origin, a loopback neighbour's Origin, an Origin equal to a loopback Host, other fetch-metadata values, a Host that agrees with a foreign Origin and an unknown method refused, a refusal running nothing; the configured Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin alone passing; /health and /.well-known outside the guard; a path no route matches answering a bare 404 whatever its signal), session_fixation, cross_persona_unlinkability, golden_wire, field_errors (a blank or missing create title, or one the name rule refuses, refused at #/title with its own code and fixed detail, nothing persisted), commission_rename (PATCH /commissions/{id}/title on the in-memory stores: the whole renamed commission, every name-rule refusal at #/title for the owner and a Participant who isn't the owner alike, a refused title answering a stranger byte for byte as it answers a made-up id, the path's id over the body's, one 404 for a stranger and a made-up id, the cross-site guard), commission_path_id (a malformed {id} on PATCH …/title and GET …/changelog — plain text, a colon, a DID, markup — answers byte for byte like a well-formed id that names nothing, never echoing it; signed out, 401 whatever the id), commission_rename_log (its own binary, the capture its global subscriber: a rename, accepted or refused, logs no title and no DID or handle at info or above), commission_writes_postgres (create and rename on PostgreSQL answer the row as stored, createdAt at the stored precision; a non-owner Participant gets 403; a stranger's rename answers byte for byte like a made-up id and like their changelog read, the problem naming no instance), den_golden (writes and drift-checks contract/golden/den), contract_current, e2e, postgres_setup (the app on PostgreSQL via test_support::pg_app), den (the den routes on the in-memory fixture world, a twin's `nameOrdinal` on its listing entry, its node and the crumb below it, and no `nameOrdinal` key anywhere else) and den_postgres (the same routes on PostgreSQL over test_support::pg_app::den_world, the one 404 for every pair of causes, and scripts/den-fill.sh filling a signed-in user's Den through the routes), commission_reads_postgres (the changelog read and the download behind den's check on PostgreSQL: each pair of not-found causes answers byte for byte alike and reads alike), den_postgres_accounts (identity's Accounts through the Den on PostgreSQL: a deactivated Account only to its Owner, equal store calls for another's and a missing Account, no answer naming another user, a refused stored name shown as its handle in the Den and served as its handle by GET /accounts and a handle change while its row keeps the text, founding refusing it with the 422, and founding accepting a `/`, which the Den names by the Account's handle; a role grant never seating a stranger and only re-roling an existing member; and a revoke or leave racing a transfer never leaving an Account without an Owner, through a stale role read over test_support::store_doubles), account_served_name (the account routes on the in-memory stores serve a stored name as the rule keeps it or as the handle, never as-is), not_found_statements (every pair of not-found causes at the same depth runs the same SQL statements in the same order, read off the wire by test_support::pg_app's statement proxy, from a warm and a cold profile cache; a board card of a stranger's Private commission and of a made-up id run the same statements, ending in commission/standing then commission/view_grant, which a Participant's card reads too; a stranger's rename and a made-up id's each run exactly session/load then commission/standing, no unit opened), not_found_timing (ignored: each read pair's clock times for the security review from a warm and a cold profile cache, then the rename's pair, interleaved and warm, with each cause's median, p10 and p90 and the pass rule's verdict: each p10 at or below the other's p90, the medians under 5% of the smaller apart; `just den-timing`), identity_reads_behind_den (GET /accounts and GET /me behind den's access check on both stacks, over test_support::store_doubles; a /me the check refuses reads no profile), dev_profile (the default-build guards in every build; with the feature, the environment lock, the fixed sign-in, sessions not crossing stacks, and the real binary, refused outside dev and beyond loopback), bug_reports (POST /bug-reports on the in-memory stores and on PostgreSQL: the session's reporter, the server's build id, absent items stored as none, a fixed 422 per field and one for a body that doesn't decode, neither echoing input, the 429, a 60-post burst storing exactly ten (from a fresh reporter, and racing for the last report behind a held users row lock on PostgreSQL), the cookie surface's Origin check and no-store, and no route that reads a report), plus CLI/API parity tests create_account_parity/delete_account_parity/whoami_parity) + tests/common/mod.rs assert_problem

notes: Cross-persona unlinkability: no route may join one person's separate handles/Users as the same human (holds by construction — separate handle → separate User → separate DID); guarded by `tests/cross_persona_unlinkability.rs`.
The cookie surface also carries `Cache-Control: no-store` (beyond CSRF) so authenticated identity/PII JSON is never cached (CWE-525).

Logging (`src/logging.rs`): `main` installs `logging::subscriber(env, filter, stdout)` — the filter is `RUST_LOG` when set and readable, else the profile's `log_level` (`ChosenFilter`; boot logs which at info) — with `composition::logging`'s filter layer on top, which drops every event from the DNS client's crates (`hickory_resolver`, `hickory_net`, `hickory_proto`) whatever the filter says, because hickory logs the name it was asked about (a handle's domain) at `error` on a malformed answer. In DEV every span prints its close with its timing (`FmtSpan::CLOSE`); in STG and PROD no span event prints and a `LevelFilter::INFO` layer caps every event at info whatever `RUST_LOG` says, so DIDs and handles at debug stay dev-only (the dev-logs ruling, 2026-10-13: debug generous in dev only; tokens, cookies, session ids, keys and passwords never logged). The dev profile's `log_level` is info for dependencies and debug for every Zurfur crate in the server's closure, pinned by `logging/tests.rs` against `cargo metadata`. `tests/log_canary.rs` drives a whole signed-in visit on PostgreSQL under the DEV subscriber at trace (sign-in, `/me`, founding an Account, bug reports, the Den root and its accounts folder, two commissions created with one title, the commissions listing, the newer twin opened as a Den node, its rename, logout) and fails on any planted secret in the capture, and on the user's DID or handle on an info-or-above line. The CLI layers the same DNS filter.

`src/generated/*.rs` still carries DD pointers in its doc comments: it is generated from `contract/*.proto`, so the fix belongs on the `.proto` field comments, not here — a hand-edit would be regenerated away.

The log canary's visitor thread (`tests/log_canary.rs`): the visitor's own HTTP client runs in the same process, and its libraries log what a browser holds (`cookie_store` every `Set-Cookie`, `reqwest` each URL with its query). The test body is the visitor and runs on the runtime's main thread, while the server runs on the workers, so a thread-local flag and a `filter_fn` keep the visitor's thread out of the capture once the server is up. The server is captured whole; its dependency tree has no `cookie_store`. `LOG_CANARY_DUMP=<file>` writes the capture for a reviewer.
